chunks: He said: Abu Ubaydillah Muhammad ibn Imran al-Marzbani reported to me, he said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Jawhari narrated to us, he said: Haroon ibn Ubaydillah al-Muqri narrated to us, he said: Uthman ibn Saeed narrated to us, he said: Abu Yahya al-Tamimi narrated to us, from Katheer, from Abu Maryam al-Khawlani, from Malik ibn Dhamrah who said: I heard Ali, the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), saying:

Be it known to you that you will be subjected to cursing me and calling me a liar. Whoever curses me unwillingly, under coercion, God knows that he was forced, and I shall arrive with him together before Muhammad, peace be upon him and his progeny. And whoever restrains his tongue and does not curse me, he will race ahead of me like the fling of an arrow or a wink of the eye. And whoever curses me with a cheerful heart, for him there is no veil between him and God, and he shall have no excuse before Muhammad, peace be upon him and his progeny.

Be it known that Muhammad, peace be upon him and his progeny, held my hand one day and said: Whoever has sworn allegiance on these five [fingers] and then died loving you, has completed his pledge. And whoever dies hating you, dies a death of pre-Islamic ignorance, and will be held accountable for what he did in Islam. And if he lives after you while loving you, God shall seal his days with security and faith, for as long as the sun rises or sets.

key_terms.لعن: La'n - Cursing; the Umayyad rulers instituted cursing Ali from pulpits
key_terms.ميتة جاهلية: Death of Jahiliyyah - dying without recognizing legitimate authority
key_terms.نحب: Nahb - Pledge, from Quran 33:23 regarding fulfilling one's covenant

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about those forced to curse him during the Umayyad era?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) foretells a time when people will be compelled to curse him, distinguishing three categories: those forced (forgiven), those who restrain their tongues (who will precede him swiftly to the Prophet), and those who curse willingly (who face God's wrath). He then relates a prophetic tradition where the Prophet (SAWW) declared that love or hatred for Ali determines one's fate. This sermon was delivered in anticipation of the Umayyad policy of cursing Ali from the pulpits.
